source_citation: Liao CT, Lin TY, Iyer HK (2005). Technometrics 47(3):323-335. doi:10.1198/004017005000000102. Example 3 (section 5.4): NIST RECIPE example 4 data; printed canonical-form inputs (sse 8663.776 on 63 df; q2..q6 1796.312, 1587.788, 11.492, 4538.396, 3231.697; eigenvalues 4.093, 5.407, 6.650, 11, 11.778 with multiplicities 1, 1, 1, 3, 1), GPQ lower (0.90, 0.95) limits 314.661 ... 301.511 and Vangel (1996) MLS limits 286.895 ... 274.784 at x0 = -67, -50, -25, 0, 25, 50, 75
tolerance: canonical form: printed 3 dp exactly (eigenvalues, multiplicities, sse, q_i); engine pivot = same chi-square to 1e-8; GPQ limits: no pass/fail (regression pin 1e-6 on the package values)
notes: Same model: H'ZZ'H of X = (1, temp), Z = batch indicators reproduces every printed canonical value, and the engine's L'CL has eigenvalues 1 / lambda_i with Q_i = q_i / lambda_i. Package GPQ (M = 20000, seed 2005) at -67 is 284.43, next to Vangel's 286.895 (and Hoffman 2010, ems/anova-mls). The printed GPQ limits are ~30 higher and lie above the plug-in 10th percentile of N(mu, sigma_a^2 + sigma_e^2) at the REML fit (~302-305), which a 95% lower confidence limit cannot do; a re-implementation of the paper's own steps with its printed canonical inputs and a cell-mean WLSE center gives ~282 at -67. Conclusion: an error in the printed GPQ values of this example, not a different model.
